cards.explanation: The answer is everyone, friends. Paul, the apostle writing to Timothy, doesn't draw a fence around this prayer list. He says petitions, prayers, intercessions and thanksgiving are to be offered for everyone (1 Timothy 2:1). That's a longer list than the line outside my bakery on a Saturday morning.

The group is kings and all those in authority, friends. Right after saying everyone, Paul names kings and all those in authority (1 Timothy 2:2). Think about that for a second. Praying for the people in charge is on Paul's list, and I bet that's a stretch some days.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says to pray for kings and all those in authority, “…so that we may lead tranquil and quiet lives in all godliness and dignity.” (1 Timothy 2:2). The text gives that reason itself, so we don't have to guess. Tranquil and quiet. Somebody write that on my oven door.

Good and pleasing, that's Paul's word for it, friends. He says praying for everyone, kings included, is good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior (1 Timothy 2:3). Two words, and no fine print. That's about as clear as a recipe gets.

The answer is False, and the verse is clear. Paul says God our Savior wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Timothy 2:4). It's not a select few. Everyone is the word, and that's why the prayer list is so big.
The mediator is the man Christ Jesus, friends, exactly as Paul says. There is one God, and one mediator between God and men (1 Timothy 2:5). One, not a committee. That's Paul's whole point.

The word is ransom, friends. Paul says Christ Jesus gave Himself as a ransom for all (1 Timothy 2:6). Jesus used that word about Himself too: “…to give His life as a ransom for many.” (Mark 10:45). It's a big word, and it's the heart of this whole passage.

Paul wants that praying without anger or dissension, friends. He wants the men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or dissension (1 Timothy 2:8). Hands up, grudges down. I've burned a batch or two when I was grumpy, so I get it.

The answer is good deeds, friends. Paul wants the women to be adorned with good deeds, as is proper for women who profess to worship God (1 Timothy 2:10). Braids, gold, pearls and expensive clothes get set aside for this. Good deeds are the outfit he points to.

The pair is teaching and exercising authority over a man, friends. Paul says, “I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; she is to remain quiet.” (1 Timothy 2:12). Both things are in the same sentence, so it's one to read slowly. Nice and careful, everybody.

The answer is True. Paul says, “For Adam was formed first, and then Eve.” (1 Timothy 2:13). The man was formed first (Genesis 2:7), and the woman was made after (Genesis 2:22). Paul states it plainly and I'll leave it as he says it.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says, “And it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman who was deceived and fell into transgression.” (1 Timothy 2:14). He names the woman as the one deceived. Careful reading, everybody.

The word is faith, friends. Paul says women will be saved through childbearing, “…if they continue in faith, love, and holiness, with self-control.” (1 Timothy 2:15). Faith leads the list, and it's the first thing he names. Keep an eye on that little word if.
